title: पुलांगु प्याखं-इकुनप्याखं
authors: महर्जन Maharjan, जीवन कुमार Jeevan Kumar
nepali: नेपालभाषाय्‌ प्याखं धाय्‌बले नाटक व नृत्य नितां कःघाः । नेपालय्‌ देवदेवीया प्याखं भाव नृत्यं शुरु जुयाः लिपा नृत्य नापनापं मे हालीगु विकास जुजुं बुलुहं नाटकया रूप काःगु खः । देवदेवीया प्याखं ख्वाःपाः पुयाः हुइगु खः । लिपा तिनि संवादया विकास जुल । थथे प्याखं दकलय्‌ न्हापां भाव नृत्यं शुरु जुयाः लिपा संवादतक विकास जूगुलिं हे प्याखं धाय्‌बले नाटक व नृत्य नितां कःघाःगु जुइमाः । तान्त्रिक शक्तिया मू स्रोतकथं पूजाआजा यानावयाचोंपिं पीठगण द्यःयात मूर्ति जक थापना यानाः मगानाः उगु मूर्ती जीवन्यास विधिं देवत्व प्रतिस्थापन याय्‌धुंकाः तिनि व द्यःया सजीवता दइगु विश्वास जूगुलिं थीथी देवदेवीयात सजीवता बीगु झोलय्‌ मनूया शरीरदुने द्यः दुबिकेगु परम्परा न्ह्यात । थुगु हे परम्परादुने थीथी मातृकायात नं सजीवता बीगु ज्या जुल । थ्व हे झोलय्‌ इकुनप्याखं दय्‌केगु ज्या जुल जुइ । तान्त्रिक शक्तिलिसे स्वापू दुगु अजिमा प्याखंत मल्लकालीन इलय्‌ इकुनप्याखंया नामं म्हसीका वयाचोंगु खः । इकुनप्याखंया नामं परिचित प्याखंत थौंकन्हे थीथी नामं म्हसीकाः वयाचोंगु दु ।
american_english: In Nepal Bhasa, the term pyakhan encompasses both drama and dance. In Nepal, the pyakhan of gods and goddesses originated from expressive dance, and later, as singing songs developed alongside dancing, it gradually assumed the form of drama. The pyakhan of gods and goddesses was performed wearing masks. Only later did dialogue develop. Because pyakhan thus began first with expressive dance and later developed up to dialogue, that must be why the term pyakhan embraces both drama and dance. Since merely installing statues of the Pithagana deities—who have been worshipped as the primary source of Tantric power—was not sufficient, and because it was believed that the deity gains living presence only after establishing divinity in the statue through the Jivanyasa rite, in the process of endowing various deities with living presence, the tradition began of invoking the deity into the human body. Within this very tradition, bringing various Matrikas to life was also carried out. It must have been in this very progression that Ikunpyakhan was created. The Ajima dances associated with Tantric power came to be known by the name of Ikunpyakhan during the Malla period. The dances known by the name of Ikunpyakhan are recognized by various names today.
